title: Attention kernel handshake orchestrator for v2/v3 compatibility
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce an explicit "handshake" orchestration layer that coordinates kernel choice between FlashAttention v2 and v3 at stream boundaries and during prefill->decode transitions. The goal is to eliminate oscillations and correctness edge cases observed when the runtime opportunistically switches kernels mid-session, and to provide deterministic fallbacks when v3 heuristics produce tail-latency regressions for long-context streaming workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic handshake state machine implemented and unit-tested
Canary rollout shows <=1% increase in 99th tail latency and >=0% change in median across representative prompt mixes
Telemetry emitted: kernel_switch_count, handshake_state_transitions, kv_epoch_mismatch, backoff_trigger_count
Automatic fallback to pinned-safe-kernel when kv_epoch_mismatch > 0 for a stream
Runbook documented and dashboard available for on-call
steps: Spec: define handshake states (UNDECIDED, V2_ACTIVE, V3_ACTIVE, STICKY_BACKOFF, FALLBACK) and transition rules
Implement per-stream handshake context with epoch tracking for KV cache alignment
Add sticky timers and exponential backoff to avoid repeated flip-flop within a single session
Emit telemetry events and create Grafana panels for switch rates and latency deltas
Integration tests with mock kernels to simulate mid-prefill and mid-decode switches
End-to-end canary: 5% fleet, 24h run, compare against control group for throughput and tail latency
If canary passes, staged rollout to 25/50/100% with monitoring windows

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Handshake adds per-request state and slight CPU overhead. Mitigation: keep handshake context extremely compact and only enable for kernels that require cross-epoch coordination; measure CPU cost in canary.
Risk: Incorrect epoch detection could force unnecessary fallbacks. Mitigation: conservative mismatch detection and hysteresis; log mismatch with samples for offline analysis.
Risk: Interference with existing warmup heuristics. Mitigation: integrate with warmup manager and add config flags to control precedence.
